shots.visual_event: Elias reveals the engine door opens only for a passenger who pays a memory equal to the person they most want to save.
Arin holds his cracked badge as it plays his oldest memory: toddler Meera asleep on his shoulder during a monsoon blackout.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “If I give this, will I know her?”

shots.visual_event: Through the train window, Meera understands and presses her palm to the glass, choosing not to stop him.
shots.dialogue_audio: Meera: “You taught the city my name.”

shots.visual_event: Arin inserts the badge. Meera’s face drains from his memories into the lock; the engine door opens.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “Take the memory. Not my choice.”

shots.visual_event: Meera stands before him, but he looks at her as a stranger; Tick projects the twelve witness memories around her.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “I don’t remember you.” Meera: “You don’t have to do it alone.”

shots.visual_event: Arin takes her hand based on trust rather than recognition and leads her into the engine.
shots.dialogue_audio: Arin: “Tell me who we are while we run.”
